name: Paladin
summary: Paladins stand between the innocent and those who would harm them. They wear heavy plate, mend the wounded and strike down the wicked with arms and the Holy Light. Humans and dwarves bear the Silver Hand's legacy in the Alliance. In the Horde, Forsaken who served the Light in life still answer its call, though it burns them.

sections.title: Origins in Lordaeron
sections.body: Archbishop Alonsus Faol formed the paladins during the Second War. After the First War left the pious Clerics of Northshire devastated, he saw that healers alone could not stand against orcish warfare. He gathered virtuous knights of Lordaeron and taught surviving clerics to fight with weapons and divine magic. Under Uther the Lightbringer, the Knights of the Silver Hand defended bodies and renewed spirits across humanity's kingdoms.

sections.title: Champions of the Holy Light
sections.body: Priests speak for the Holy Light, preaching faith and tending to common folk's spirits. Paladins take up arms in its name. Their conviction lets them strengthen allies with auras, seal blessings upon them and mend fatal wounds. Against unholy horrors, the Light courses through their blows and burns undead and demonic foes with righteous fury.

sections.title: Heirs of the Silver Hand
sections.body: The fall of Lordaeron in the Third War scattered the original order, but its ideals endure. Humans in the south and dwarves of Ironforge have taken up its mantle. In sanctuaries such as the Cathedral of Light and the Hall of Mysteries, they train and pledge sword and shield to justice. They defend the Alliance against gathering shadows.

sections.title: Paladins of the Forsaken
sections.body:
Some knights of Lordaeron returned from the grave as Forsaken. Those who served the Light in life still keep their vows, and it still answers them, though each prayer sears their dead flesh. Aramis Hammerhand trains the risen paladins in the chapel at Deathknell, while Shari Stilwell continues their instruction in Brill.

Tyr's Watch, an order of Forsaken paladins, holds Bandarion Keep in western Tirisfal. Their path is lonely. They wield the power that burned their people, and Sylvanas Windrunner tolerates the order while watching it closely.

faq.q: What is the difference between a priest and a paladin?
aliases: how are paladins different from priests
faq.answer: Priests speak for the Light and guide the faithful through prayer and ritual. Paladins wear heavy plate and wield weapons in its name, defending the weak and enforcing divine justice in battle.

Archbishop Alonsus Faol created the order during the Second War. After the Clerics of Northshire were slain in the First War, he gathered devout knights and trained surviving clerics to join martial discipline with holy magic as the Knights of the Silver Hand.

Humans and dwarves serve as paladins in the Alliance, while Forsaken do so in the Horde. The order began among humans, Ironforge's dwarves embraced the Holy Light, and some Forsaken who were knights or clerics in life still wield it after death, though it brings constant pain.

faq.q: Why are paladins effective against the undead?
aliases: why does holy magic hurt undead
faq.answer: The Holy Light opposes necrotic corruption and demonic energy. Paladins channel it to purge blight and burn unholy creatures, making them foremost champions against the Scourge and other foul beings.

faq.q: What happened to the original Knights of the Silver Hand?
faq.answer: The plague devastated Lordaeron during the Third War, and the original order suffered grievous losses. Betrayal and political strife fractured the brotherhood, but surviving members and new initiates in Stormwind and Ironforge carry its title and ideals forward. Some fallen knights rose again as Forsaken and still keep their oaths.

faq.q: Can members of the Horde become paladins?
faq.answer: Only Forsaken become paladins within the Horde. Many were knights or clerics of Lordaeron before the plague, and some still keep their vows; the Light answers them, though it burns their dead flesh. Orcs, tauren and trolls follow shamans, druids and witch doctors rather than the knightly way of the Holy Light.

faq.q: Why does the Light hurt Forsaken paladins?
aliases: does the light hurt undead paladins
faq.answer: The Holy Light opposes the dark energy that sustains the undead. A Forsaken paladin's faith and will let them channel it, but the Light burns dead flesh and reawakens deadened nerves. Each blessing and heal brings searing pain, which their trainers teach them to endure as proof that the Light still answers.

angles.text: As a novice paladin, you follow Uther the Lightbringer and Alonsus Faol, joining readiness for battle to an oath of selfless duty.
As a priest, you share a deep spiritual bond with paladins. You guide the faithful through sermons and faith, while they shield them with steel.
As a dwarf of Ironforge, you have embraced the tenets of the Silver Hand, whose discipline of the Light fits your unyielding nature.
As a human, you carry the enduring soul of the Alliance as a paladin, keeping alive the sacred crusade forged in the horrors of the Second War.
As an Alliance paladin, you rally troops with sacred auras and kindle hope across the battlefield.
As a Forsaken, you may be one of the rare risen paladins, a knight who kept your vows beyond death and still wields the Light, paying for every prayer in pain.
As a member of the Horde, you know that only the Forsaken raise paladins, and even among your own people the order meets suspicion.
